title: Project Hail Mary
creator: Andy Weir
notes: A junior-high science teacher wakes up light-years from home with amnesia and humanity's fate on his shoulders. Problem-solving sci-fi at its most fun.

title: good kid, m.A.A.d city
creator: Kendrick Lamar
notes: A concept album disguised as a mixtape: one long night in Compton, sequenced like a film. Short film, bonus disc, and all.

title: The West Wing
creator: Aaron Sorkin
notes: Sorkin's walk-and-talks remain the most flattering — and most instructive — portrait of public service ever filmed.

title: I, Pencil
creator: Leonard Read
notes: A pencil explains its own creation and dismantles central planning in four pages. A classic, and absurdly short.

title: Loonshots
creator: Safi Bahcall
notes: Why sane teams dismiss the crazy ideas that change everything — and how phase transitions in organizations mirror them in physics.

title: Diplomacy
creator: Henry Kissinger
notes: A sweeping tour of statecraft from Richelieu to the Cold War. Heavy, but worth every page.

title: The Federalist Papers
creator: Hamilton, Madison & Jay
notes: Hamilton, Madison, and Jay sell the Constitution in real time.

title: Basic Economics
creator: Thomas Sowell
notes: Prices, incentives, and trade-offs with zero equations and endless common sense. Working through it slowly.

title: The Theory of Money and Credit
creator: Ludwig von Mises
notes: Mises integrates money into economic theory and predicts the perils of inflation a century early. On the stack.

title: The Man in the High Castle
creator: Frank Spotnitz
notes: The Axis won. A prestige series that makes authoritarianism feel mundane — and resistance feel costly.

title: Why We Disagree About Inequality
creator: Ilana Redstone
notes: Dueling definitions of fairness keep both sides talking past each other — and how to finally have the conversation.

title: Conversations with Tyler
creator: Daron Acemoglu
notes: Acemoglu asks whether liberalism's crisis was an inside job — and implicates the educated elite.

title: EconTalk
creator: Ben Southwood
notes: Southwood argues the Industrial Revolution really began in 1688, when England's Glorious Revolution smashed the vetocracy holding growth back.

title: The 2026 Midterm Forecast
creator: Nate Silver
notes: Polls, fundamentals, and probabilities for a Congress worth watching.

title: Illmatic
creator: Nas
notes: Ten tracks, a decade of Queensbridge compressed into forty minutes. Still the reference point.
